nodes.content: Design an ownership type checker for cancellable asynchronous tasks that safely transfer borrowed resources across task boundaries.
requirements: Guarantee memory safety under cancellation and task migration without whole-program analysis or runtime borrow checks.
Accept 12 safe and reject 12 unsafe programs covering nested borrows, ownership transfer, and cancellation.

nodes.content: Use region-indexed nurseries, affine move/borrow captures, transitive lifetime constraints, Send migration bounds, and uncancellable child draining on scope exit.
When cancellation starts during a nested reborrow, which nursery must retain the original lender until the borrowing grandchild finishes?
The lender's owning nursery drains transitive borrowing descendants before releasing it, even when cancellation reaches an intermediate task.
Specify descendant-drain ordering, implement region-constraint propagation, and test nested reborrows under cancellation in a 24-program suite.
Model-check DrainTree-3 cancellation and migration schedules for three-level reborrows, asserting lender destruction follows every borrowing descendant’s completion.
DrainTree-3 found cancellation after sibling-nursery handle transfer destroyed the lender before its migrated borrowing grandchild finished.
Require lender nurseries to adopt migrated borrowers’ join obligations before transfer and drain them before releasing the lender.
Rerun DrainTree-3 with statically adopted join obligations across sibling transfers, checking lender-drop order under every cancellation schedule.
DrainTree-3 explored 1,284 cancellation schedules; adopted join obligations prevented premature lender drops in every schedule.
Adopt static join-obligation transfer for cross-nursery handles: it fixes the sibling-transfer counterexample and passed all 1,284 DrainTree-3 schedules.
Implement region-constraint checking with adopted join obligations, then compile Borrow24’s 12 safe and 12 unsafe cancellation/migration programs.
Borrow24 v0.1 contains a region-constraint checker with adopted join obligations and 24 annotated programs covering reborrows, transfers, and cancellation.
Which Send constraints permit borrower migration when the lender stays pinned and its destructor requires the original thread?
Test 16 Borrow24 migration variants for shared/unique Send bounds, pinned lenders, and origin-thread destruction across workers.
Borrow24 v0.1 accepted 3/16 unsafe migrations: two shared Cell borrows raced, and one pinned lender dropped off-thread.
Require `T: Sync` for migrating `&T`, `T: Send` for `&mut T`, and origin-affine nursery drops for pinned lenders.
Implement migration bounds and origin-affine drops, prove modular cancellation safety, verify Borrow24’s 12 safe, 12 unsafe, and 16 migration variants.
Patch Borrow24 v0.1 with Sync/Send migration checks and origin-affine drop scheduling; rerun its 24 annotated programs.
Borrow24 v0.2 implements migration bounds and origin-affine drops; its regression report records 12 safe accepts and 12 unsafe rejects.
Compare Borrow24 v0.1 and v0.2 across 24 annotated programs and 16 migration variants, checking acceptance labels and destructor-thread traces.
Borrow24 v0.2 accepted 12/12 safe programs, rejected 12/12 unsafe programs, and eliminated v0.1’s three unsafe migration acceptances.
Keep v0.2 migration bounds and origin-affine drops: they remove all three v0.1 violations without regressing Borrow24’s 24 labeled programs.
Mechanize small-step preservation for region-indexed nurseries with adopted joins, Send/Sync migration bounds, and origin-affine drops under arbitrary cancellation.
Mechanized preservation proves adopted joins with Send/Sync bounds and origin-affine drops prevent dangling borrows under cancellation and migration.
How must executor shutdown coordinate origin-affine drops when migrated borrowers outlive the origin worker?
Executor shutdown must keep origin workers alive until all adopted borrower joins finish and origin-affine destructor queues drain.
Model-check Borrow24 v0.2 shutdown in ShutdownTrace-48, asserting origin-worker retirement follows adopted joins and destructor-queue drainage.
ShutdownTrace-48 found 3 late-drop schedules: after joins and queue drainage, deferred cancellation cleanup enqueued origin-affine destructors onto retired workers.
Add a shutdown barrier that quiesces cancellation cleanup before draining destructor queues, while origin workers remain active.
What shutdown state transition prevents deferred cleanup from enqueueing origin-affine drops after the barrier declares quiescence?
Extend Borrow24’s join obligations with atomic cleanup-registration closure; model-check active cleanup completion before origin-affine destructor drainage.
ShutdownTrace-48 found zero late drops after atomic registration closure; all 48 schedules retired workers only after cleanup and drop drainage.
Atomically closing cleanup registration, then awaiting registered cleanup before destructor drainage, prevents post-quiescence origin-affine enqueueing.
Model-check ShutdownTrace-256 racing cleanup registration against shutdown, asserting no origin-affine enqueue occurs after cleanup completion and queue drainage.
ShutdownTrace-256 exposed 2 late drops: registered cleanup spawned untracked deferred finalizers that enqueued origin-affine drops after queue drainage.
Atomically seal root cleanup registration; track deferred finalizers through inherited counted tokens, draining drops only after every token retires.
Rerun ShutdownTrace-256 with inherited finalizer tokens, checking token-count zero precedes destructor drainage and origin-worker retirement.
ShutdownTrace-256 verified 256/256 schedules: inherited tokens covered deferred finalizers, with zero late drops or premature worker retirements.
Adopt inherited finalizer tokens: registration closure passed 48 schedules but failed 2/256; tokenized shutdown passed 256/256.
Implement Borrow24 v0.3: atomically seal root registration, await inherited finalizer tokens, drain origin drops, then retire workers.
Borrow24 v0.3 adds tokenized shutdown and origin-worker retirement ordering; its regression suite includes ShutdownTrace-256 and 24 annotated programs.
Introduce compositional task-effect signatures recording borrowed regions, transferable joins, Send/Sync bounds, and shutdown-token obligations for separate compilation.
How can task-effect signatures track deferred finalizers spawned by higher-order cleanup callbacks across separately compiled modules?
Compile 18 higher-order cleanup fixtures separately against Borrow24 v0.3, checking signature obligations against deferred-finalizer shutdown traces.
Callback signatures with finalizer-token effects classified 18/18 separate-module fixtures; signatures omitting those effects admitted two late-drop cases.
Extend exported task signatures with polymorphic callback finalizer-token effects, check substitutions locally, then rerun 18 separate-module fixtures.
Implement polymorphic finalizer-token effects in exported callback signatures and locally check substitutions across the 18 separate-module fixtures.
Borrow24 v0.4 exports polymorphic callback effects and verifies finalizer-token obligations at module boundaries without runtime borrow checks.
Constrain detached tasks to owned static captures; make borrowed task handles affine and reject escapes beyond their lender’s nursery.
Add detach typing and affine-handle escape checks, then test borrowed versus owned static captures across cancellation and migration.
Implement static-owned detach and affine-handle escape checks atop Borrow24 v0.4; test 20 migration/shutdown cases with exported callback effects.
Borrow24 v0.5 adds static-owned detach rules and affine borrowed handles; its fixture pack contains 20 annotated migration/shutdown cases.
Run 20 detach/escape fixtures through Borrow24 v0.5, checking diagnostic classifications and migrated-task shutdown traces.
Borrow24 v0.5 accepted 10/10 owned-static detaches and rejected 10/10 borrowed detach or handle-escape cases.
Can an owned-static detached task retain an origin-affine resource after shutdown retires its original worker?
Probe 12 Borrow24 v0.5 owned-static detach fixtures with origin-affine destructors, task migration, and worker shutdown before task completion.
Three of 12 owned-static detaches retained origin-affine values past worker retirement, leaving no valid thread for their destructors.
Detached tasks may retain origin-affine values safely if counted worker leases prevent retirement until their destructors finish.
Preserve v0.5’s 20 detach/escape classifications, add counted origin-worker leases, and rerun the 12 origin-affine detach fixtures.
Instrument Borrow24 v0.5 detached tasks with counted origin-worker leases; rerun 12 affine-drop fixtures and 20 detach/escape regressions.
Borrow24 v0.6 revises v0.5 detachment with counted origin-worker leases and regression fixtures for affine drops and handle escapes.
Model-check v0.6 worker retirement against lease counts across 12 origin-affine detaches, then verify 20 detach/escape classifications.
Borrow24 v0.6 prevented premature retirement in 12/12 affine-drop fixtures and preserved all 20 detach/escape classifications.
Adopt leased detachment: v0.5 classified 20 cases but stranded three affine drops; v0.6 passed all 12 and retained classifications.
